title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 13
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 13: a third visit announced, the call to examine yourselves, power through weakness, and the closing greeting.

questions.text: By how many witnesses shall every word be established, as this chapter quotes it?
questions.explanation: Announcing his third visit, the writer quotes that at the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.

questions.text: What does he say beforehand about coming again?
questions.explanation: He writes beforehand to those who have sinned and to all the rest that, if he comes again, he will not spare.

answers.text: That he will stay only briefly
That he will send others first
That he will say nothing at all

questions.text: Through what does the chapter say Christ lives, after being crucified through weakness?
questions.explanation: It says he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives through the power of God.

answers.text: Through the faith of the assembly
Through the witness of the apostles

questions.text: What does the writer tell the readers to do about themselves?
questions.explanation: He tells them to examine their own selves, whether they are in the faith, and to test their own selves.

answers.text: Keep silent until he writes again
Examine and test their own selves

questions.text: What does he pray to God for them?
questions.explanation: He prays that they do no evil, not so that he may appear approved, but that they may do what is honorable.

questions.text: What does he say about what they can do against the truth?
questions.explanation: He says that they can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth.

answers.text: They can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth
They must defend the truth with letters
They can hide the truth for a time
They will be judged by the truth alone

questions.text: After saying they rejoice when they are weak, what does he say they pray for?
questions.explanation: He says they rejoice when they are weak and the readers are strong, and they also pray for the readers becoming perfect.

answers.text: For his own release from prison

questions.text: Why does he write these things while he is absent?
questions.explanation: He writes while absent so that he may not deal sharply when present, according to the authority the Lord gave him for building up and not for tearing down.

answers.text: So that others may read the letter first
So that he may not deal sharply when present
So that he need not come at all
So that his words may be kept as a record

questions.text: How are the readers told to greet one another?
questions.explanation: After telling them to rejoice, be comforted and live in peace, he tells them to greet one another with a holy kiss.

questions.text: What three things does the closing verse ask to be with them all?
questions.explanation: The letter closes by asking that the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, God's love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with them all.

answers.text: Grace, love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit
Faith, hope, and love that never ends
Wisdom, power, and riches of glory
